summary: For every finite simple graph G, the robust clique covering number theta_1(G) (the maximum, over 1-selections in which each vertex selects one incident edge, of the clique covering number after deleting the selected edges) equals the clique covering number theta(G) if and only if G has no edges. This is Conjecture 1 of the source, proved without the isolate-free hypothesis of the MathDB record. The argument modifies the proofs of Proposition 7 and Theorem 6 of the source by an explicit 1-selection. Significance is modest: a short argument on a question the source authors left open.

title: The strict lower-bound conjecture for the robust clique covering number
source: Gábor Bacsó, Balázs Patkós, Zsolt Tuza and Máté Vizer, “The robust chromatic number of graphs”, arXiv:2305.01923 (2023). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01923)
statement: Let $G$ be an isolate-free graph. Write $\theta(G)$ for its clique covering number and $\theta_1(G)$ for the corresponding robustness parameter, so that the general lower bound is $\theta_1(G)\geq\theta(G)$. **Strict lower-bound conjecture.** The inequality is strict unless $G$ is edgeless; equivalently, equality can occur only for edgeless graphs. This conjecture asks for a characterization of the equality case in the lower bound for the robust clique covering number. Its status is not established in the supplied source.
